title: Norah Jones: Come Away With Me Album Review | Pitchfork
quote: The 23-year-old singer-songwriter had just swept the lauded Big Four categories for her debut album, Come Away With Me; over the previous year, her gentle rasp of a voice floated out of seemingly every Starbucks, wine tasting room, and parents’ CD changer.

title: Amy Winehouse: Back to Black Album Review | Pitchfork
quote: "They tried to make me go to rehab," wails Amy Winehouse on the opening track and first single from her second album Back to Black.

title: Daft Punk: Random Access Memories Album Review | Pitchfork
quote: They’ve come a long way since, but the playfulness remains, and so does their ability to surprise. Random Access Memories, the fourth proper studio album from Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, continues the trend.

title: Taylor Swift: 1989 Album Review | Pitchfork
quote: Her first four albums hinge on that feeling, full of vivid, sprawling documents of failed romances that left her gasping for air, wondering how to be someone her lovers would miss.

title: Taylor Swift: Folklore Album Review | Pitchfork
quote: One of the loveliest tracks on Folklore, the surprise album the singer-songwriter made primarily with the National’s guitarist, Aaron Dessner, stands out for a strangely similar reason: a thread connecting two strangers that exists long before either realizes it’s there.

title: Harry Styles: Harry’s House Album Review | Pitchfork
quote: Five years ago, in the run-up to his debut album, Harry Styles got that quintessential rock’n’roll treatment: A sprawling 6,000 words by the celebrated journalist and filmmaker Cameron Crowe.

title: Taylor Swift: Midnights Album Review | Pitchfork
quote: Midnights is Swift’s first album to be recorded entirely with Jack Antonoff, after nearly a decade of ever higher-profile collaborations. In the past, he has accentuated Swift’s ambitiously vivid storytelling with expressive, technicolor synth pop.
